scenario: An application on EC2 needs to read objects from an S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant access?

options.text: Attach an IAM role with an S3 read policy to the instance profile
Store an IAM user's access keys in the application config
options.note: Long-term keys can leak and must be rotated manually.

options.text: Make the bucket public and restrict access by obscure object names
options.note: Public buckets expose data to anyone.

options.text: Embed the root account's access keys in the instance user data
options.note: Never use root credentials for applications.

explanation: Instance profiles deliver temporary credentials from STS that rotate automatically. Grant least privilege in the role's policy.

scenario: A company wants to require MFA for all console users and stop anyone from using the root account day to day. What should be done with the root user?

options.text: Enable MFA, delete its access keys, use it only when required
Share its password with the admin team for emergencies
options.note: Shared root credentials are a major risk.

options.text: Delete the root user once IAM administrators exist
options.note: The root user can't be deleted.

options.text: Create access keys for it so scripts can run with full rights
options.note: Root access keys should not exist.

explanation: Lock away the root user with MFA and no access keys. Use IAM Identity Center or IAM roles for daily administration.

scenario: An IAM policy allows s3:* on a bucket, but an SCP attached to the account denies s3:DeleteObject. Can the user delete objects?

options.text: No, because an explicit deny in the SCP overrides the allow
Yes, because identity policies take priority over SCPs
Yes, because s3:* includes every action automatically
Only if the user signs in with MFA first
options.note: MFA doesn't override an SCP deny.

explanation: Evaluation logic: explicit deny anywhere wins. SCPs set the maximum permissions for accounts in an organization; they don't grant anything.

scenario: A company with 40 AWS accounts wants to prevent any account from disabling CloudTrail. What is the best control?

options.text: An SCP in AWS Organizations that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and DeleteTrail
An IAM policy in each account that denies the actions to all users
options.note: Admins in each account could remove it.

options.text: An AWS Config rule that sends an email when a trail is stopped
A CloudWatch alarm on the trail's log volume dropping to zero

explanation: SCPs act as guardrails that even account administrators (including root in member accounts) can't bypass.

scenario: Developers in Account A need to manage resources in Account B without creating IAM users in Account B. What should be used?

options.text: An IAM role in Account B that trusts Account A, assumed with STS
Copies of the Account B root credentials stored in Secrets Manager
A VPC peering connection between the two accounts
options.note: Network connectivity doesn't grant API access.

options.text: An S3 bucket policy that lists the developers' user names
options.note: Only covers one bucket, not account resources.

explanation: Cross-account access uses a role whose trust policy names the other account. Users call sts:AssumeRole to get temporary credentials.

scenario: A company wants employees to sign in to multiple AWS accounts with their existing corporate identities. Which service fits best?

options.text: AWS IAM Identity Center connected to the corporate identity provider
Separate IAM users in every account with matching passwords
Amazon Cognito user pools for the internal staff
options.note: Designed for app end users, not workforce access to AWS.

options.text: AWS Directory Service Simple AD in every account

explanation: IAM Identity Center provides workforce single sign-on with permission sets across all accounts in an organization.

scenario: A mobile app needs users to sign up and sign in, then upload photos directly to S3. Which combination fits?

options.text: Cognito user pools plus identity pools for temporary credentials
An IAM user created for each app user during sign-up
A shared access key compiled into the mobile app binary
options.note: Keys can be extracted from the app.

options.text: IAM Identity Center permission sets assigned to each customer
options.note: Built for workforce, not app users.

explanation: User pools handle authentication; identity pools exchange tokens for scoped, temporary AWS credentials.

scenario: What is the purpose of a permissions boundary on an IAM role?

options.text: It caps the permissions the role's policies can grant
It grants extra permissions on top of the role's policies
It limits which IP addresses can assume the role
options.note: That's a condition in a policy.

options.text: It applies the same limits to every account in the organization

explanation: Effective permissions are the intersection of identity policies and the boundary. Boundaries help delegate role creation safely.

scenario: An S3 bucket must only be accessible to requests from a specific VPC endpoint. Which policy condition key is used?

options.text: aws:SourceIp with the VPC's CIDR range
options.note: Private IPs aren't seen through endpoints this way.

options.text: s3:x-amz-acl set to private in the policy

explanation: aws:SourceVpce (or aws:SourceVpc) in a bucket policy restricts access to traffic arriving through a gateway or interface endpoint.

scenario: A company must make sure no S3 bucket in an account can ever be made public by mistake. What is the simplest control?

options.text: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level
Review every bucket policy and ACL by hand each week
Enable default SSE-KMS encryption on every bucket
Turn on S3 Versioning and MFA Delete for all buckets

explanation: Block Public Access settings override any policy or ACL that would grant public access. New buckets have it enabled by default.

scenario: Which S3 encryption option lets the company control and audit the key, including when it's used?

options.text: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
SSE-S3 with Amazon S3 managed keys
options.note: AWS manages keys; no per-key control or audit.

options.text: Client-side encryption with no key logging
options.note: No AWS-side audit of key usage.

options.text: S3 Object Lock in governance mode

explanation: Customer managed KMS keys allow key policies, rotation settings and CloudTrail logging of every key use.

scenario: An S3 bucket uses SSE-KMS. Requests are being throttled during a heavy upload job. What can reduce KMS calls?

options.text: Enable S3 Bucket Keys for the bucket
Switch the bucket to S3 Standard-IA
options.note: Storage class doesn't affect KMS calls.

options.text: Turn off versioning for the bucket
Increase the bucket's object size limit

explanation: S3 Bucket Keys generate a bucket-level data key, cutting KMS requests and cost by up to 99%.

scenario: Compliance requires that financial records in S3 can't be deleted or overwritten by anyone, including the root user, for 7 years. What should be used?

options.text: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a 7-year retention period
S3 Object Lock in governance mode with a 7-year retention period
options.note: Users with special permissions can bypass governance mode.

options.text: A bucket policy that denies s3:DeleteObject to all users
options.note: An admin could change the policy.

options.text: S3 Versioning with MFA Delete turned on
options.note: Protects deletes, but root can still remove versions with MFA.

explanation: Compliance mode can't be shortened or removed by any user. Object Lock requires versioning.

scenario: A partner needs to download one private S3 object for the next hour without an AWS account. What is the best approach?

options.text: Generate a presigned URL that expires in one hour
Make the object public, then make it private later
Create an IAM user for the partner with S3 access
Email the object's ARN to the partner

explanation: Presigned URLs use the signer's permissions and expire automatically.

scenario: Static website content in a private S3 bucket must only be served through CloudFront. What should be configured?

options.text: Origin access control with a bucket policy that allows it
Public bucket access with a CloudFront cache policy
S3 Transfer Acceleration enabled on the bucket
An S3 gateway endpoint in the default VPC

explanation: OAC (the successor to OAI) signs requests to S3, and the bucket policy allows only the distribution.

scenario: A database password used by Lambda must rotate automatically every 30 days. Which service fits best?

options.text: AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation
Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameters
An encrypted environment variable on the Lambda function
A KMS key with automatic key rotation enabled

explanation: Secrets Manager can rotate secrets on a schedule using built-in or custom rotation functions, including for RDS.

scenario: What happens when automatic rotation is enabled on a customer managed KMS key?

options.text: New key material yearly; old material kept for decryption
All existing data is re-encrypted with the new material
The key ID and ARN change each time the key rotates
Old key material is deleted once rotation completes

explanation: KMS keeps previous key material so older ciphertext still decrypts. Applications don't need changes.

scenario: An EBS volume must be encrypted, but the existing unencrypted volume can't be encrypted in place. What is the correct process?

options.text: Snapshot, copy the snapshot encrypted, create a new volume
Enable encryption on the volume while it's detached
options.note: Can't encrypt an existing volume in place.

options.text: Turn on account-level EBS encryption and reboot
Change the volume type from gp2 to gp3 with encryption

explanation: Encrypted copies of snapshots create encrypted volumes. Enable EBS encryption by default for new volumes.

scenario: Which service provides dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules that the customer fully controls?

options.text: AWS KMS with AWS managed keys

explanation: CloudHSM gives FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSMs in your VPC. KMS can use CloudHSM as a custom key store.

scenario: A public website on an Application Load Balancer needs a free, auto-renewing TLS certificate. What should be used?

options.text: A self-signed certificate uploaded to IAM
AWS CloudHSM with a generated key
A KMS asymmetric key attached to the ALB

explanation: ACM public certificates are free for integrated services like ALB and CloudFront and renew automatically.

scenario: Which statement about security groups is correct?

options.text: They're stateful, so return traffic is allowed automatically
They're stateless and need explicit rules for return traffic
They support both allow and deny rules
options.note: Security groups only have allow rules.

options.text: They're applied at the subnet level only

explanation: Security groups are stateful and allow-only. Network ACLs are stateless, support deny rules and apply to subnets.

scenario: A specific malicious IP address must be blocked from reaching all instances in a subnet. Which control fits?

options.text: A network ACL deny rule for that IP
A security group deny rule for that IP
A route table blackhole to that IP
options.note: Not the right tool for inbound filtering.

options.text: An IAM policy denying the IP address

explanation: NACLs evaluate rules in number order and support explicit deny. For web apps, AWS WAF IP sets are another option.

scenario: A web tier security group should accept traffic only from the load balancer. What is the best rule?

options.text: Allow the app port from the ALB's security group
Allow the app port from 0.0.0.0/0 with a NACL
Allow the app port from the ALB's public IP
Allow all ports from the VPC's CIDR range

explanation: Referencing a security group as a source allows any ENI in that group, even as IPs change.

scenario: A web application must be protected from SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Which service should be used?

options.text: AWS WAF on the ALB or CloudFront distribution
Security groups with stricter port rules
AWS Shield Standard on the VPC
options.note: Protects against DDoS, not SQL injection.

explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP(S) requests using managed and custom rules, including SQLi and XSS rule sets.

scenario: A company needs protection against large DDoS attacks, plus 24/7 access to the AWS Shield Response Team. Which service fits?
explanation: Shield Standard is automatic and free. Shield Advanced adds enhanced detection, cost protection and the SRT.

scenario: Instances in private subnets must download software updates from the internet but must not accept inbound connections from it. What is needed?

options.text: A NAT gateway in a public subnet and a route to it
An internet gateway route in the private subnet
A VPC peering connection to a public VPC
options.note: Peering isn't transitive to the internet.

options.text: Elastic IP addresses on each private instance

explanation: NAT gateways allow outbound IPv4 connections only. For IPv6, use an egress-only internet gateway.

scenario: Private instances need to call the S3 API without traffic going over the internet or through a NAT gateway. What is the lowest-cost option?

options.note: Works, but has hourly and data charges.

options.text: A NAT gateway with a route to S3

explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free and added as targets in route tables.

scenario: A SaaS provider wants to expose its service privately to customer VPCs without VPC peering. What should it use?

options.text: AWS PrivateLink with an NLB-backed endpoint service
A transit gateway shared with every customer
A public ALB restricted by security groups
VPC peering with each customer's VPC

explanation: PrivateLink exposes a single service to consumers through interface endpoints, without exposing the provider's whole VPC.

scenario: An admin needs shell access to private EC2 instances without opening port 22 or running bastion hosts. What should be used?

options.text: A bastion host in a public subnet
EC2 Instance Connect with a public IP
options.note: Requires port 22 and a reachable IP.

options.text: A NAT gateway with port forwarding

explanation: Session Manager uses the SSM Agent and IAM, logs sessions, and needs no inbound ports.

scenario: Which service continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to detect threats such as compromised instances?
explanation: GuardDuty is a managed threat detection service that needs no agents for its core log sources.

scenario: A company must find personally identifiable information stored in S3 buckets. Which service fits?
explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover sensitive data such as PII in S3.

scenario: Which service scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities?
explanation: Inspector automatically and continuously scans workloads for CVEs and network exposure.

scenario: Security wants a record of every API call made in all accounts, stored centrally and protected from tampering. What should be configured?

options.text: An organization trail logging to a locked-down S3 bucket
VPC Flow Logs enabled in every VPC and account
CloudWatch metrics and alarms for each service
AWS Config recording in a single account
options.note: Records configuration, not every API call.

explanation: Organization trails cover all member accounts. Enable log file validation and restrict access to the log bucket.

scenario: A company must detect when any security group allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 and automatically fix it. What is the best approach?

options.text: An AWS Config rule with automatic remediation
A monthly manual audit of security groups

options.note: Reports but doesn't remediate rule changes.

explanation: Config evaluates resources against rules and can trigger Systems Manager Automation documents to remediate.

scenario: A security team wants one dashboard that aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie across accounts. Which service fits?
explanation: Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes findings and runs security standard checks.

scenario: A company must centrally manage AWS WAF rules and security group policies across all accounts in its organization. Which service fits?

options.note: A stateful VPC firewall, not central policy for WAF.
Sets up landing zones and guardrails.

explanation: Firewall Manager applies WAF, Shield Advanced, security group and Network Firewall policies across an organization.

scenario: A company is setting up many new AWS accounts and wants a governed multi-account environment with preventive and detective controls. What should it use?

options.note: Deploys stacks, not a governed landing zone.

explanation: Control Tower builds a landing zone on Organizations with controls (guardrails), account factory and centralized logging.

scenario: Resources in one account should be shared with other accounts in the organization, such as subnets or Transit Gateways. Which service is used?

options.text: Service control policies in AWS Organizations

explanation: RAM shares resources like subnets, Transit Gateways and Route 53 Resolver rules across accounts.

scenario: An RDS database must be encrypted at rest, but it was created without encryption. How can it be encrypted?

options.text: Snapshot, copy it encrypted, and restore a new instance
Modify the instance and enable encryption in place
options.note: Can't enable encryption on an existing instance.

options.text: Enable TLS on all client connections to the instance
options.note: Encrypts in transit, not at rest.

options.text: Create an encrypted read replica of the unencrypted instance
options.note: A replica of an unencrypted instance can't be encrypted.

explanation: Encryption must be set at creation. Restore from an encrypted snapshot copy, then switch over.

scenario: Clients must only connect to an RDS for PostgreSQL database using TLS. How is this enforced?

options.text: Set the rds.force_ssl parameter in the DB parameter group
Use a security group rule that allows port 443 only
Enable encryption at rest with KMS

explanation: Parameter groups control engine settings. MySQL uses require_secure_transport for the same purpose.

scenario: Users should access an RDS MySQL database using IAM credentials instead of database passwords. What should be enabled?

options.note: For app users, not database auth.

explanation: IAM database authentication issues short-lived tokens in place of passwords for MySQL and PostgreSQL.

scenario: A DynamoDB table holds sensitive data. Which statement about its encryption is correct?

options.text: All tables are encrypted at rest by default
Encryption must be enabled when the table is created
Only global tables can be encrypted
Encryption requires DAX to be enabled

explanation: DynamoDB encrypts all data at rest. You can choose an AWS owned key, an AWS managed key or a customer managed key.

scenario: An API Gateway REST API must accept only requests from users signed in through a Cognito user pool. What should be configured?

options.text: A Cognito user pool authorizer on the API methods
A resource policy allowing all IP addresses
API keys sent in each request
options.note: API keys identify clients but aren't authentication.

explanation: API Gateway supports IAM, Cognito and Lambda authorizers. Use usage plans and API keys for throttling, not auth.

scenario: Sensitive configuration values used by EC2 applications should be stored centrally and encrypted at no extra cost for standard use. What fits?

options.text: Plaintext config files in a private S3 bucket
EC2 user data scripts at launch
options.note: Visible to anyone who can describe the instance.

explanation: Standard SecureString parameters are encrypted with KMS and have no storage charge. Use Secrets Manager when you need rotation.

scenario: A Lambda function must access resources in a private subnet of a VPC. What is required?

options.text: Attach the function to the VPC's subnets and a security group
Assign an Elastic IP address to the function's ENI
Use a public subnet with an internet gateway
options.note: Doesn't connect it to private resources.

options.text: Run it on a Dedicated Host inside the VPC

explanation: VPC-attached functions use Hyperplane ENIs in your subnets. Add a NAT gateway or endpoints if they also need AWS APIs or internet.

scenario: A company needs a stateful, managed network firewall with intrusion prevention to inspect traffic between VPCs and the internet. Which service fits?

options.text: AWS WAF on the internet gateway
options.note: WAF attaches to web resources, not IGWs.

explanation: Network Firewall supports stateful rules, domain filtering and Suricata-compatible IPS rules.

scenario: VPC Flow Logs are enabled. What information do they capture?

options.text: Traffic metadata: IPs, ports, protocol, accept/reject
Full packet payloads for deep packet inspection
API calls made by IAM users

explanation: Flow logs capture metadata about traffic at the VPC, subnet or ENI level and publish to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose.

scenario: A company uses AWS Organizations and wants to stop all accounts from launching resources outside us-east-1 and eu-west-1. How?

options.text: An SCP denying requests outside approved aws:RequestedRegion values
An IAM policy on each user listing the approved Regions
options.note: Hard to manage; admins could change it.

options.text: AWS Config rules that delete resources in other Regions
Disabling the other Regions in the Billing console
options.note: Default Regions can't be disabled this way.

explanation: Region-deny SCPs commonly exempt global services such as IAM, CloudFront and Route 53.

scenario: Which is the correct way to give a Lambda function permission to write to a DynamoDB table?

options.text: Grant dynamodb:PutItem in the function's execution role
Add the function's ARN to the table's ACL
Store an IAM user's access keys in an environment variable
Enable DynamoDB Streams with the function as a trigger
options.note: Streams send changes out; they don't grant access.

explanation: Lambda assumes its execution role. Resource-based policies on the function control who can invoke it.

scenario: An S3 bucket receives uploads from many accounts. The bucket owner needs to own every object automatically. What setting should be used?

options.text: Object Ownership set to bucket owner enforced
Requester Pays enabled on the bucket
S3 Object Lock in governance mode
Same-Region Replication to a second bucket

explanation: Bucket owner enforced disables ACLs, so the bucket owner owns all objects and access is controlled by policies.

scenario: A team must allow temporary, federated access to the AWS console for contractors using SAML 2.0. What is required in IAM?

options.text: A SAML identity provider and a role that trusts it
An IAM user per contractor with a console password
A Cognito user pool with the hosted sign-in UI
One access key pair shared by all of the contractors

explanation: SAML federation maps IdP users to IAM roles via sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML. IAM Identity Center can simplify this.

scenario: Which statement about S3 bucket policies and IAM policies is correct?

options.text: Within one account, either policy can allow access if nothing denies it
Both must allow the request, even within the same account
options.note: Either is enough within one account.

options.text: Bucket policy allows always override IAM policy denies
IAM policies can't reference S3 buckets or objects

explanation: Within one account, an allow in either policy is enough. Cross-account requests need an allow on both sides.

scenario: A company needs to inspect encrypted east-west and north-south traffic using third-party firewall appliances. Which service simplifies deploying them at scale?
explanation: Gateway Load Balancer uses GENEVE to send traffic transparently through fleets of virtual appliances.

scenario: An application must prove that log files in S3 haven't been modified after CloudTrail delivered them. What should be enabled?
explanation: Validation creates signed digest files so you can detect modification or deletion of log files.

scenario: A web app on EC2 should block requests from specific countries. What is the simplest option?

options.text: An AWS WAF geographic match rule
Network ACL rules for every IP range in those countries
Security groups that deny those countries

explanation: WAF geo match rules (or CloudFront geo restriction) block or allow requests by country.

scenario: A data lake in S3 needs fine-grained, column-level permissions for analysts using Athena. Which service manages this?
explanation: Lake Formation centrally governs permissions on Glue Data Catalog tables down to column and row level.

scenario: An EC2 instance's metadata service should be protected from SSRF-based credential theft. What should be enforced?

options.text: A public IP on the instance

explanation: IMDSv2 requires a PUT request for a session token, which blocks most SSRF attacks. Set HttpTokens to required.

scenario: A company connects on-premises users to AWS using AWS Client VPN. What does this provide?

options.text: Managed OpenVPN-based remote access for users
A dedicated private fiber connection to a VPC
A content delivery network for private content

explanation: Client VPN is a managed remote-access VPN. Site-to-Site VPN connects networks; Direct Connect provides private links.

scenario: An account's IAM users keep creating overly permissive policies. Which tool can find resources shared outside the account and validate policies?
explanation: Access Analyzer identifies external access, validates policies against best practices and can generate least-privilege policies.

scenario: An order service sends work to a processing service that sometimes slows down, causing lost requests. What is the best way to decouple them?

options.text: Put an Amazon SQS queue between the services
Call the processing service synchronously with retries
Increase the instance size of the order service
Store requests in instance memory until processed

explanation: SQS buffers messages durably, so producers and consumers scale and fail independently.

scenario: Messages must be processed exactly once and in the order they were sent. Which queue type should be used?
explanation: FIFO queues support ordering per message group and exactly-once processing with deduplication.

scenario: An SQS consumer takes up to 4 minutes to process a message, and other consumers keep picking up the same message. What should be changed?

options.text: Raise the visibility timeout above the processing time
Decrease the message retention period to 4 minutes
options.note: Affects how long messages stay in the queue.

options.text: Enable long polling on the queue
Switch to an SNS topic with one subscriber

explanation: The visibility timeout hides a message while it's being processed. The default is 30 seconds; the maximum is 12 hours.

scenario: Messages that fail processing repeatedly should be moved aside for later analysis. What should be configured?

options.text: A dead-letter queue with a redrive policy
A shorter visibility timeout on the queue
Message deduplication IDs on each message
A delay queue with a 15-minute delay

explanation: After maxReceiveCount failed receives, SQS moves the message to the DLQ. You can redrive it back later.

scenario: One event must be delivered to three different SQS queues for independent processing. What is the best pattern?

options.text: Publish to an SNS topic that the three queues subscribe to
Have the producer write to each queue separately
options.note: Couples the producer to every consumer.

options.text: Use one queue polled by three consumer services
options.note: Each message goes to only one consumer.

options.text: Use an SQS FIFO queue with three message groups

explanation: SNS-to-SQS fan-out delivers a copy of each message to every subscribed queue.

scenario: Events from SaaS applications and AWS services must be routed to different targets based on their content. Which service fits best?

options.text: Amazon EventBridge rules with event patterns
Amazon SQS standard queues with long polling
options.note: Queues don't filter by content to multiple targets.
Streaming; consumers do their own filtering.

explanation: EventBridge routes events from AWS services, SaaS partners and custom apps to targets using rules.

scenario: A multi-step order process with retries, error handling and human approval must be coordinated. Which service fits?

options.text: Amazon SQS with a single queue
A cron job on an EC2 instance

explanation: Step Functions state machines handle sequencing, retries, parallel branches and wait-for-callback steps.

scenario: A web application runs on EC2 in one Availability Zone. How should it be made highly available?

options.text: An Auto Scaling group across AZs behind an ALB
Use a larger instance type in the same AZ
options.note: Still a single point of failure.

options.text: Add a second ENI and Elastic IP to the instance
Take hourly EBS snapshots of the instance

explanation: Spreading instances across AZs with health checks lets the ALB and Auto Scaling route around failures.

scenario: An RDS MySQL database must fail over automatically if the primary's Availability Zone fails. What should be enabled?

options.text: A read replica in the same AZ
options.note: Same AZ, and promotion is manual.

explanation: Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in another AZ and fails over automatically by updating the DNS endpoint.

scenario: What is a key difference between RDS Multi-AZ and read replicas?

options.text: Multi-AZ: synchronous, for availability; replicas: async, for reads
Read replicas fail over automatically; Multi-AZ doesn't
Multi-AZ standby instances serve read traffic by default
options.note: The classic standby doesn't serve reads.

options.text: Read replicas can only be created in the same AZ
options.note: They can be cross-AZ or cross-Region.

explanation: Multi-AZ DB clusters (two readable standbys) also exist, but the classic Multi-AZ instance standby isn't readable.

scenario: Which Aurora feature provides the fastest failover with a readable copy in the same Region?

options.text: Daily automated snapshots restored on failure
Aurora Backtrack to a point before the failure

explanation: Aurora storage is replicated six ways across three AZs. Aurora Replicas share the storage and are failover targets.

scenario: A global application needs a relational database with fast cross-Region disaster recovery and low-latency reads in multiple Regions. What fits?

options.text: Daily snapshots copied to another Region

explanation: Aurora Global Database replicates with typically under one second of lag and supports managed failover to a secondary Region.

scenario: A DynamoDB-backed application needs active-active writes in multiple Regions. What should be used?

options.text: DynamoDB Streams with Lambda copying to another table

explanation: Global tables replicate automatically across Regions with multi-active writes.

scenario: Requests for /api should go to one target group and /images to another. Which load balancer supports this?

options.text: Application Load Balancer with path-based rules
Network Load Balancer with TCP listeners

options.note: DNS can't route by URL path.

explanation: ALBs route on path, host, headers, query strings and source IP.

scenario: An application needs a load balancer with static IP addresses per AZ and extremely high TCP throughput. Which should be used?

options.note: A CDN, not a TCP load balancer.

explanation: NLBs handle millions of requests per second at layer 4 and support Elastic IPs per AZ.

scenario: An Auto Scaling group should replace instances that fail application health checks, not just EC2 status checks. What should be configured?

options.text: Enable ELB health checks on the Auto Scaling group
Increase the health check grace period to 1 hour
Use a larger instance type for both

explanation: With ELB health checks, instances marked unhealthy by the load balancer are terminated and replaced.

scenario: Traffic increases sharply every weekday at 9 AM. How can Auto Scaling have capacity ready before the spike?

options.text: A scheduled scaling action before 9 AM
A simple scaling policy with a long cooldown
Increasing the health check grace period

explanation: Scheduled actions change capacity at set times. Predictive scaling can also forecast recurring patterns.

scenario: An Auto Scaling group should keep average CPU near 50%. Which policy type is simplest?
explanation: Target tracking adjusts capacity automatically to keep a metric at the target value.

scenario: Users lose their sessions when requests hit a different instance behind an ALB. What is the most scalable fix?

options.text: Store session state in ElastiCache or DynamoDB
Enable sticky sessions with very long durations
options.note: Unbalanced load and lost sessions on failure.

options.text: Store sessions on each instance's EBS volume

explanation: Stateless app tiers with an external session store scale and survive instance failures.

scenario: A company needs the lowest-cost DR strategy and can accept recovery taking many hours. Which fits?
explanation: DR strategies from cheapest/slowest to most expensive/fastest: backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, multi-site active-active.

scenario: A DR plan keeps the database replicating to another Region with app servers off until needed. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Pilot light keeps core data live and starts compute during recovery.

scenario: What does RPO measure?

options.text: The maximum acceptable data loss, in time
The total cost of the DR solution per year
The number of Regions used for recovery

explanation: RPO (recovery point objective) is about data loss; RTO (recovery time objective) is about downtime.

scenario: Backups of EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB and EFS must be managed centrally with policies and copied to another Region. Which service fits?
explanation: AWS Backup uses backup plans, vaults, cross-Region and cross-account copies, and Vault Lock for immutability.

scenario: Physical and virtual servers on premises need block-level replication to AWS for fast recovery. Which service fits?
explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates servers and launches recovery instances in minutes.

scenario: S3 objects must be copied automatically to a bucket in another Region for disaster recovery. What is required?

options.text: Versioning on both buckets plus Cross-Region Replication
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archive tiers
Create a lifecycle rule that moves objects to Glacier

explanation: Replication requires versioning on source and destination. Existing objects need S3 Batch Replication.

scenario: Traffic should go to a primary site, and to a secondary site only if the primary's health check fails. Which Route 53 routing policy fits?
explanation: Failover routing uses health checks to direct traffic to the secondary record when the primary is unhealthy.

scenario: Users should be routed to the Region that gives them the lowest network latency. Which Route 53 policy fits?

options.note: Based on location, not measured latency.

explanation: Latency routing uses AWS latency measurements between users and Regions.

scenario: A new application version should receive 10% of traffic while the old version receives 90%. Which Route 53 policy fits?
explanation: Weighted records split traffic by relative weight.

scenario: A zone apex (example.com) must point to an ALB. Which record type should be used?

options.note: CNAMEs aren't allowed at the zone apex.

explanation: Alias records work at the apex, map to AWS resources and have no query charge for AWS targets.

scenario: A global application needs static anycast IP addresses and fast failover between Regional endpoints. Which service fits?

options.note: No static anycast IPs for the app.

explanation: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IPs and routes over the AWS backbone, failing over in seconds.

scenario: Several EC2 instances across AZs need a shared POSIX file system that grows automatically. What fits?

options.text: An EBS volume shared by Multi-Attach
Amazon S3 mounted with a script

explanation: EFS is a regional, elastic NFS file system accessible from multiple AZs.

scenario: Which statement about EBS volumes is correct?

options.text: An EBS volume is tied to one Availability Zone
EBS volumes are replicated across Regions
EBS volumes can attach to instances in any AZ
EBS data is lost when the instance stops

explanation: Use snapshots to move volumes across AZs or Regions.

scenario: What happens to data on an EC2 instance store volume when the instance is stopped?

options.text: It's kept until the instance starts again
It's copied to an EBS snapshot automatically

explanation: Instance store data survives reboots but not stop, hibernate or termination.

scenario: Windows applications need a shared SMB file system with Active Directory integration. Which service fits?
explanation: FSx for Windows File Server supports SMB, NTFS, AD integration and Multi-AZ deployments.

scenario: On-premises applications need low-latency access to frequently used files while all data is stored in S3. What fits?
explanation: File Gateway presents NFS/SMB shares on premises, caches recent data locally, and stores objects in S3.

scenario: A company wants to run containers without managing EC2 instances or clusters of servers. What fits?

options.text: Amazon ECS or EKS with AWS Fargate
EC2 Auto Scaling groups with Docker

explanation: Fargate is serverless compute for containers; you define task CPU and memory.

scenario: A Lambda function processes SQS messages, and some batches fail repeatedly. How can only the failed messages be retried?

options.note: More messages would be retried together.

options.text: Increase the function timeout to one full hour
Switch the function to an SNS trigger instead

explanation: Partial batch responses return only the failed message IDs, so successful messages aren't reprocessed.

scenario: What is the maximum execution time for an AWS Lambda function?
explanation: For longer work, use Step Functions, ECS/Fargate or AWS Batch.

scenario: An API must handle unpredictable spikes without managing servers. Which architecture fits best?

options.text: API Gateway with Lambda and DynamoDB
A single EC2 instance with a database
EC2 Reserved Instances sized for peak
A Classic Load Balancer with fixed instances

explanation: Serverless services scale automatically and are highly available by default across AZs.

scenario: A Lambda function sometimes overwhelms a downstream database during spikes. What limits the number of concurrent executions?

options.text: A larger memory setting for the function
A shorter timeout on each invocation

explanation: Reserved concurrency guarantees and caps concurrency. Placing SQS in front also smooths spikes. RDS Proxy pools connections.

scenario: Lambda functions open too many connections to an RDS database. What should be used?

options.note: A cache, not a connection pool.

explanation: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, improving scalability and failover times.

scenario: Which Auto Scaling feature keeps a pool of pre-initialized instances to reduce scale-out time?

options.note: Pause instances during launch or terminate.

explanation: Warm pools keep stopped or running instances ready, reducing latency for apps with long boot times.

scenario: An application must keep processing if one AZ fails, with no capacity loss. The Auto Scaling group needs 6 instances during normal load across 3 AZs. What should the minimum be?
explanation: To survive one AZ loss with 6 remaining, each of the remaining 2 AZs needs 3, so 3 per AZ across 3 AZs = 9.

scenario: A stream of clickstream events must be processed by multiple consumers, replayed within 7 days, and kept in order per key. Which service fits?
explanation: Kinesis Data Streams keeps ordered records per shard (24 hours by default, up to 365 days) for multiple consumers.

scenario: A VPC needs to connect to 50 other VPCs and on-premises networks with transitive routing. What should be used?

options.text: A NAT gateway in each VPC

explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub with route tables, supporting VPCs, VPNs and Direct Connect.

scenario: A company needs a dedicated private network link to AWS with a backup in case it fails. What is a cost-effective design?

options.text: Direct Connect primary with a Site-to-Site VPN backup
Two Site-to-Site VPNs with no Direct Connect
One Direct Connect connection with no backup
An internet gateway as the backup path

explanation: VPN over the internet is a common low-cost backup for Direct Connect. For maximum resilience, use multiple DX locations.

scenario: An application should keep running when EC2 instances are replaced, so no data should be stored only on the instances. Which principle is this?
explanation: Store state in managed services (S3, DynamoDB, RDS, ElastiCache) so instances are disposable.

scenario: A workload must keep running if a whole AWS Region fails. Which design meets this?

options.text: Two Regions with replicated data and DNS failover
Deploy across three AZs in one Region
Use Reserved Instances in the primary Region
Use larger EBS volumes with more snapshots

explanation: Multi-Region designs need replicated data (Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB global tables, S3 CRR) and DNS or Global Accelerator failover.

scenario: Which statement about S3 durability and availability is correct?

options.text: S3 Standard: 11 nines of durability across 3+ AZs
S3 One Zone-IA stores data across three AZs
S3 Standard stores data in a single AZ by default
S3 durability depends on enabling versioning
options.note: Versioning protects from deletes, not durability.

explanation: S3 Standard: 99.999999999% durability, 99.99% availability design. One Zone-IA is lower-cost and stored in one AZ.

scenario: Lambda functions invoked asynchronously sometimes fail. How can failed events be captured for later processing?

options.text: Configure an on-failure destination or a DLQ
Enable X-Ray tracing on the function

options.note: Changes the pattern; caller must retry.

explanation: Async invocations retry twice by default, then send to an on-failure destination (SQS, SNS, Lambda, EventBridge) or DLQ.

scenario: An application uses ElastiCache for Redis OSS as a session store. How can it survive a node failure?

options.text: Multi-AZ with a replica and automatic failover
Use Memcached with a single large node
Increase the node size of the primary
Store sessions in memory on the app servers

explanation: Redis OSS replication groups with Multi-AZ promote a replica automatically if the primary fails.

scenario: A database on EC2 needs consistent, very high IOPS (over 100,000) with sub-millisecond latency on EBS. Which volume type fits?
explanation: io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS per volume. gp3 provides a 3,000 IOPS baseline, configurable up to 80,000 (raised from 16,000 in September 2025).

scenario: A log-processing workload reads large files sequentially and needs high throughput at low cost. Which EBS volume type fits?
explanation: st1 is for frequently accessed, throughput-intensive workloads like big data and log processing. HDD volumes can't be boot volumes.

scenario: Which change lets a gp2 volume's IOPS be set independently of its size, often at lower cost?

options.note: Shares a volume; doesn't change IOPS.

options.text: Take a snapshot and restore it

explanation: gp3 decouples IOPS and throughput from size and is about 20% cheaper per GB than gp2.

scenario: Users worldwide upload large files to an S3 bucket in one Region, and uploads are slow. What should be enabled?

options.text: S3 Requester Pays on the bucket

explanation: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations. Multipart upload parallelizes large objects (recommended above 100 MB).

scenario: An HPC workload needs a high-performance file system that integrates with S3 for input data. Which service fits?
explanation: FSx for Lustre provides sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s, and can link to S3 buckets.

scenario: An EFS file system serves many clients with spiky throughput needs. Which throughput mode scales automatically with workload?

options.note: Affects latency/IOPS scaling, not throughput mode.

explanation: Elastic throughput automatically scales up and down with the workload and is recommended for spiky or unpredictable use.

scenario: A tightly coupled HPC application needs the lowest network latency between instances. Which placement group strategy fits?

options.note: For large distributed systems like HDFS.

options.text: No placement group with larger instances

explanation: Cluster placement groups pack instances close together in one AZ for low latency and high throughput.

scenario: A small set of critical instances must each run on separate hardware to reduce correlated failures. Which placement strategy fits?

options.text: Partition placement group with one partition

explanation: Spread placement groups put each instance on distinct racks, up to 7 instances per AZ per group.

scenario: Which EC2 instance family is optimized for memory-intensive workloads like in-memory databases?
explanation: Families: C compute, R/X memory, M general purpose, I/D storage, P/G/Inf accelerated, T burstable.

scenario: An application's EC2 instances need higher network performance and lower latency. What should be enabled?
explanation: The Elastic Network Adapter provides up to hundreds of Gbps on supported instance types. EFA adds OS-bypass for HPC.

scenario: Which compute option fits short, event-driven tasks that run for a few seconds and scale from zero?
explanation: Lambda scales automatically per request and bills per millisecond of execution.

scenario: A batch job needs thousands of containers and compute instances scheduled and scaled automatically. Which service fits?
explanation: AWS Batch manages job queues and provisions EC2, Spot or Fargate capacity based on job requirements.

scenario: An RDS MySQL database is overloaded by reporting queries that only read data. What should be added?

options.note: The classic standby doesn't serve reads.

options.text: A larger storage volume with more IOPS

explanation: Point reporting tools at the read replica endpoint to offload the primary.

scenario: Frequently read data from DynamoDB must be returned in microseconds. What should be added?
explanation: DAX is an in-memory cache for DynamoDB, compatible with the DynamoDB API.

scenario: A web app runs the same expensive database queries repeatedly. What reduces database load and latency?

options.text: Add more storage to the database
Use a larger EBS volume for the web tier

explanation: Caching (lazy loading or write-through) serves repeated reads from memory.

scenario: A DynamoDB table has a hot partition because most requests use the same partition key. What should be done?

options.text: Use a high-cardinality, evenly accessed partition key
Switch the table to provisioned capacity mode
Enable point-in-time recovery on the table
Add a local secondary index on the same key

explanation: Distribute requests across partition keys, for example by adding a suffix (write sharding).

scenario: A DynamoDB table needs queries on an attribute that isn't part of the primary key. What should be added?

options.text: A global secondary index on it
A larger read capacity setting for scans
A second table with the same key

explanation: GSIs can use a different partition and sort key and can be added any time. LSIs must be created with the table.

scenario: A workload has unpredictable traffic on a DynamoDB table, with long idle periods. Which capacity mode fits?

options.text: Provisioned capacity with no auto scaling

explanation: On-demand mode bills per request and scales instantly. Provisioned mode with auto scaling suits predictable traffic.

scenario: Which database fits a social graph with highly connected data and relationship queries?
explanation: Neptune is a graph database supporting Gremlin, openCypher and SPARQL.

scenario: An analytics team needs to run complex SQL queries over petabytes of structured data. Which service fits?
explanation: Redshift is a columnar, massively parallel data warehouse. Redshift Spectrum queries data in S3 directly.

scenario: Analysts want to run ad hoc SQL queries directly on data in S3 without loading it anywhere. Which service fits?
explanation: Athena is serverless and charges per data scanned. Columnar formats like Parquet and partitioning reduce cost and speed queries.

scenario: Athena queries on large CSV files in S3 are slow and expensive. What improves performance most?

options.text: Convert to Parquet and partition the data
Move the data to S3 Glacier
Use larger CSV files with no partitions

explanation: Columnar, compressed formats and partitions reduce the data Athena scans.

scenario: Static assets on S3 load slowly for users around the world. What should be used?

options.text: S3 Cross-Region Replication to every Region
A larger EC2 instance as a proxy

explanation: CloudFront caches content at edge locations close to users.

scenario: A CloudFront distribution has a low cache hit ratio because each request includes unique query strings that don't change content. What should be done?

options.text: Remove unneeded query strings from the cache key
Lower the default TTL to zero seconds
Add more origins and an origin group

explanation: Cache policies control the cache key. Include only the values that change the response.

scenario: Lightweight request manipulation such as header rewrites must run at CloudFront edge locations with sub-millisecond latency. What fits?

options.note: Heavier; runs at Regional edge caches.

explanation: CloudFront Functions run on viewer events for simple, high-scale logic. Lambda@Edge supports longer and network-dependent code.

scenario: A gaming company needs to improve performance for UDP game traffic from global players to Regional servers. Which service fits?
explanation: Global Accelerator supports TCP and UDP and routes traffic over the AWS global network.

scenario: An application with users in one city needs single-digit millisecond latency for compute close to them. Which option fits?

options.text: A larger instance in the nearest Region

options.note: Data transfer and edge compute in disconnected sites.

options.text: AWS Outposts in a remote Region

explanation: Local Zones place compute and storage in metro areas. Wavelength serves 5G mobile edge; Outposts runs AWS on premises.

scenario: A company that already uses AWS Snow Family devices must move 80 TB to S3, and its internet link would take months. What is the best option?

options.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration over the existing link

explanation: Snow devices ship data physically. Note: Snowball Edge is no longer offered to new AWS customers; they should use AWS DataSync online, or AWS Data Transfer Terminals and partner solutions for offline transfers.

scenario: Files must be copied regularly from an on-premises NFS share to Amazon EFS, with encryption and integrity checks. Which service fits?

options.note: Presents S3 as a file share.

explanation: DataSync automates and accelerates online transfers between on-premises storage and AWS storage services.

scenario: Partners must upload files to S3 using SFTP without changing their clients. Which service fits?
explanation: Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP and AS2 endpoints for S3 and EFS.

scenario: Streaming data must be loaded into S3 and Redshift with minimal code and automatic batching. Which service fits?

options.text: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with custom consumers

explanation: Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) delivers streams to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch and HTTP endpoints, with optional Lambda transforms.

scenario: A team needs a managed Apache Kafka service for an existing Kafka application. Which service fits?
explanation: Amazon MSK runs Apache Kafka. Amazon MQ supports ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ for existing apps using those protocols.

scenario: Data in S3 needs ETL jobs and a central metadata catalog for Athena and Redshift Spectrum. Which service fits?

options.note: Processing, but no catalog by itself.

explanation: Glue provides crawlers, the Data Catalog and serverless Spark ETL jobs.

scenario: Business users need interactive dashboards built from Athena and Redshift data. Which service fits?
explanation: QuickSight is a serverless BI service with dashboards and natural language queries.

scenario: Logs must be searchable with full-text queries and visualized in near real time. Which service fits?
explanation: OpenSearch Service supports full-text search, log analytics and dashboards.

scenario: An API Gateway REST API returns the same responses for many requests. What reduces backend load?
explanation: API Gateway caching stores responses for a TTL (default 300 seconds).

scenario: A Lambda function has slow cold starts that affect a latency-sensitive API. What helps most?
explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps initialized execution environments ready. SnapStart helps Java, Python and .NET functions.

scenario: How can a Lambda function get more CPU power?
explanation: Lambda allocates CPU in proportion to memory (128 MB to 10,240 MB).

scenario: An SQS consumer makes many empty ReceiveMessage calls. What reduces empty responses and cost?

options.text: Use short polling with more consumers

explanation: Long polling waits for messages to arrive before returning.

scenario: Which DynamoDB read option guarantees the most recent data at the cost of more read capacity?
explanation: Strongly consistent reads use twice the read capacity of eventually consistent reads.

scenario: Which S3 feature improves request performance for very high request rates?

options.text: Use a single prefix for all objects

explanation: S3 supports at least 3,500 PUT and 5,500 GET requests per second per prefix. More prefixes scale further.

scenario: Large downloads from S3 are slow. What improves throughput from the client side?
explanation: Byte-range fetches download parts of an object in parallel and can retry failed ranges.

scenario: An application needs a fully managed, MongoDB-compatible document database. Which service fits?
explanation: DocumentDB is MongoDB API-compatible. Keyspaces is for Apache Cassandra workloads.

scenario: IoT devices send sensor readings every second, and queries focus on recent time ranges. Which database fits?
explanation: Timestream is a serverless time-series database with tiered storage.

scenario: An application needs a relational database that scales capacity automatically for unpredictable workloads. What fits?

options.text: RDS with a fixed instance class

explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales in fine-grained capacity units in seconds.

scenario: An application on EC2 writes temporary scratch data that needs extremely high I/O and can be lost. What fits best?
explanation: Instance store provides very high, low-latency local I/O on supported instance types, but data is ephemeral.

scenario: A single Kinesis data stream is throttling writes. What increases its write capacity in provisioned mode?
explanation: Each shard supports 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s of writes. On-demand mode scales automatically.

scenario: A fault-tolerant batch job can be interrupted and restarted at any time. Which EC2 purchasing option is cheapest?
explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% off On-Demand, with a two-minute interruption notice.

scenario: A database server runs 24/7 on the same instance type for the next three years. Which option gives the biggest discount with the least flexibility needed?

options.text: 3-year Standard RI or EC2 Instance Savings Plan

explanation: Longer terms and less flexibility give bigger discounts. All Upfront payment adds a little more.

scenario: A company runs EC2, Fargate and Lambda workloads and expects instance families and Regions to change. Which commitment fits?

options.note: Tied to one instance family in one Region.

explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply across instance families, sizes, Regions, OS, tenancy, Fargate and Lambda.

scenario: A licensing agreement requires software to run on a physical server whose sockets and cores are visible to the customer. What fits?

options.note: Single-tenant hardware but no socket visibility.

explanation: Dedicated Hosts support bring-your-own-license scenarios that require per-socket or per-core licensing.

scenario: Capacity must be guaranteed in a specific AZ for a short event, without a long-term commitment. What should be used?

options.text: Spot Instances with a high max price

explanation: Capacity Reservations can be created and cancelled any time and are billed at On-Demand rates whether used or not.

scenario: An Auto Scaling group runs a web tier with a steady base load and unpredictable peaks. Which mix minimizes cost while staying reliable?

options.text: Savings Plans for the base; Spot and On-Demand for peaks
All Spot Instances across several instance types
options.note: Risky if Spot capacity is reclaimed.

options.text: All On-Demand Instances with target tracking
Dedicated Hosts sized for the peak load

explanation: Auto Scaling groups support mixed instances policies with On-Demand base capacity and Spot for the rest.

scenario: A development environment is only used 9 AM–5 PM on weekdays. How can EC2 costs be reduced most simply?

options.text: Stop the instances outside working hours
Use larger instances to finish work faster

explanation: Use Instance Scheduler, EventBridge Scheduler with Systems Manager, or Auto Scaling scheduled actions.

scenario: Which tool recommends right-sizing for EC2 instances, EBS volumes and Lambda functions based on usage?
explanation: Compute Optimizer uses CloudWatch metrics and machine learning to recommend optimal resources.

scenario: Which Graviton-based instance change often reduces cost for compatible workloads?
explanation: Graviton instances commonly deliver up to 40% better price performance than comparable x86 instances.

scenario: Data is accessed frequently for 30 days, then rarely, but must be available within milliseconds when needed. What is the most cost-effective design?

options.text: S3 Standard, then lifecycle to Standard-IA at 30 days
S3 Standard for the object's whole life
S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days
S3 One Zone-IA from the day of upload

explanation: Standard-IA has lower storage cost with retrieval fees and millisecond access. The minimum storage duration is 30 days.

scenario: Access patterns for data in S3 are unknown and change over time. Which storage class fits best?
explanation: Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers automatically with no retrieval fees, for a small monitoring charge.

scenario: Compliance archives must be kept for 10 years, accessed almost never, and can tolerate 12–48 hours to retrieve. What is the cheapest class?
explanation: Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class; standard retrieval is within 12 hours and bulk within 48 hours.

scenario: Archived medical images are rarely accessed but must be retrievable in milliseconds when needed. Which class fits?
explanation: Glacier Instant Retrieval suits data accessed about once a quarter with millisecond access. Minimum storage duration is 90 days.

scenario: Easily reproducible thumbnails are accessed infrequently. Which storage class is cheapest while keeping millisecond access?

options.note: Built for high performance, not low cost.

explanation: One Zone-IA stores data in one AZ at about 20% less than Standard-IA. Use it for data that can be recreated.

scenario: Old object versions in a versioned bucket are increasing storage costs. What should be configured?

options.text: A lifecycle rule to expire noncurrent versions
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket

explanation: Lifecycle rules can transition or expire noncurrent versions and clean up incomplete multipart uploads.

scenario: Incomplete multipart uploads are using storage in a bucket. How can they be removed automatically?

options.text: A lifecycle rule to abort incomplete uploads
Turn on versioning for the bucket
Use S3 Inventory reports to list the parts

explanation: AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle actions delete parts after a set number of days.

scenario: A team wants to see which S3 prefixes use the most storage and get recommendations to reduce cost. What should be used?
explanation: Storage Lens provides organization-wide usage and activity metrics with cost-optimization recommendations.

scenario: Private instances download large amounts of data from S3 through a NAT gateway, causing high charges. What is the cheapest fix?

options.text: Add a second NAT gateway in another AZ
Move the instances into a public subnet
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration for downloads

explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no charge and avoid NAT data processing fees.

scenario: Which data transfer is generally free in AWS?

options.text: Data transferred into AWS from the internet
Data transferred out to the internet
Data processed by a NAT gateway

explanation: Inbound data transfer is free. Cross-AZ, cross-Region and internet egress have charges.

scenario: Two instances exchange a lot of data and are in different AZs, creating transfer charges. The workload doesn't need cross-AZ resilience. What reduces cost?

options.text: Place both instances in the same AZ
Use public IP addresses for the traffic
Use a larger instance type for both
Use VPC peering between the subnets

explanation: Data transfer within the same AZ using private IPs is free. Cross-AZ transfer is charged in each direction.

scenario: A company serves large media files to global users directly from S3, with high data transfer out costs. What can reduce cost?

options.text: Use S3 Glacier for the files

explanation: Transfer from S3 to CloudFront is free, CloudFront egress is often cheaper, and caching reduces origin requests.

scenario: A company runs one NAT gateway per AZ in three AZs for a dev VPC that doesn't need high availability. How can cost be reduced?

options.text: Use a single NAT gateway for the dev VPC
Replace NAT gateways with internet gateways in private subnets

explanation: Production should keep one NAT gateway per AZ for resilience; non-production can accept a single one.

scenario: A dev database is used only a few hours a day, at unpredictable times. Which option reduces cost most?
explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity with demand and can scale to 0 ACUs (auto-pause) when idle.

scenario: An RDS instance runs steadily 24/7 for production. How can its cost be reduced without changing the architecture?

options.text: Use Spot pricing for the RDS instance
Move the database to Dedicated Hosts
Add read replicas to spread the load

explanation: RDS Reserved Instances offer significant discounts for 1- or 3-year commitments. Database Savings Plans are another option.

scenario: A DynamoDB table has steady, predictable traffic. Which capacity choice minimizes cost?

options.note: Higher per-request cost for steady loads.

options.text: DAX in front of on-demand capacity

explanation: Provisioned mode is cheaper for predictable workloads; reserved capacity discounts it further.

scenario: Old items in a DynamoDB table are no longer needed after 90 days. How can they be deleted at no extra cost?

options.text: Enable TTL on an expiry attribute
Run a daily Scan and DeleteItem job
Enable point-in-time recovery on the table
Use DynamoDB Streams to delete items

explanation: TTL deletes expired items in the background without consuming write capacity.

scenario: A Lambda function's memory is set to 10 GB, but it uses 300 MB and runs quickly. What reduces cost?

options.text: Right-size memory based on measured usage
Move the function into a private VPC subnet

explanation: Lambda bills by GB-seconds. Test memory settings to find the best price-performance.

scenario: Which architecture usually costs least for a website with low, sporadic traffic?

options.text: S3 and CloudFront, with Lambda for dynamic parts
Two EC2 instances behind an ALB in two AZs
An EKS cluster with three worker nodes
A Redshift cluster as the website backend

explanation: Serverless and static hosting have near-zero idle cost.

scenario: A team stores hundreds of TB of logs in CloudWatch Logs that are rarely queried after 30 days. What reduces cost?

options.text: Set retention and export older logs to S3
Keep all logs forever in CloudWatch Logs

explanation: CloudWatch Logs retention defaults to never expire. S3 with lifecycle rules is cheaper for long-term storage.

scenario: Finance wants an alert when monthly spend is forecast to exceed $10,000. Which service fits?

options.note: Visualizes cost; alerts are in Budgets.

explanation: Budgets alerts on actual or forecasted cost and usage, and Budget Actions can apply SCPs or IAM policies.

scenario: A company wants to analyze spending trends over the last 12 months and forecast the next 3 months. Which tool fits?
explanation: Cost Explorer visualizes historical costs, forecasts, and Reserved Instance and Savings Plan recommendations.

scenario: Costs must be allocated to departments based on resource tags. What must be done?

options.text: Activate them as cost allocation tags
Create a separate VPC for each department
Enable CloudTrail data events for all resources
Use AWS Config rules to require the tags

explanation: Activated cost allocation tags appear in Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report. AWS Organizations can also separate costs by account.

scenario: A company needs to estimate the cost of a new architecture before building it. Which tool fits?
explanation: Pricing Calculator models services and configurations to estimate monthly costs.

scenario: Multiple AWS accounts should receive one bill and share volume discounts and Reserved Instance benefits. What should be used?
explanation: The management account pays for all member accounts, and usage is combined for tiered pricing and RI/Savings Plan sharing.

scenario: Which service gives the most detailed line-item billing data for analysis in Athena or QuickSight?
explanation: CUR/Data Exports deliver hourly line items to S3 for analysis.

scenario: Unattached EBS volumes and idle load balancers are adding cost. Which service flags these automatically?
explanation: Trusted Advisor checks for idle and underutilized resources. Full checks require Business Support or higher.

scenario: An application stores large files that are accessed once after upload and then deleted after 7 days. What minimizes storage cost?

options.text: S3 Standard with a 7-day expiration rule
S3 Standard-IA for all uploaded objects
EBS volumes attached to an EC2 instance

explanation: IA and Glacier classes have minimum storage durations, so short-lived objects are cheaper in Standard.

scenario: Containers in ECS run steady, long-running services. Which option usually reduces compute cost most for this pattern?

options.text: A Compute Savings Plan for the usage
Run the containers on Dedicated Hosts

explanation: Compute Savings Plans cover Fargate and EC2. Fargate Spot suits interruptible tasks.

scenario: A data warehouse is only queried a few times a week with variable workloads. Which option minimizes cost?

options.text: A large provisioned Redshift cluster running 24/7

options.note: Not a warehouse, and doubles cost.

explanation: Redshift Serverless charges for compute used (RPU-hours) and scales automatically.

scenario: Which choice reduces EBS snapshot costs for long-term retention that's rarely restored?

options.text: Move them to EBS Snapshots Archive
